title: Daemon local-auth proof verifier is not wired in the production executable
affectedAsset: ASSET-008 Computer Use approvals and high-impact local actions
description: The daemon has an independent local-auth proof verifier and regression tests showing the proof is enforced when wired. The production executable passes nil, and the RPC enforcement helper treats a nil verifier as no-op.
evidence: OpenBurnBarDaemon/Sources/OpenBurnBarDaemonExecutable/OpenBurnBarDaemonMain.swift:54-86 wires localAuthProofVerifier to nil.
OpenBurnBarDaemon/Sources/OpenBurnBarDaemon/RPC/BurnBarDaemonServer+RPCComputerUse.swift:111-132 returns nil when the verifier is absent.
OpenBurnBarDaemon/Sources/OpenBurnBarDaemon/DaemonLocalAuthProofVerifier.swift:6-18 and 100-160 implement the intended proof checks.
OpenBurnBarDaemon/Tests/OpenBurnBarDaemonTests/BurnBarDaemonComputerUseLocalAuthProofWiringTests.swift:90-225 proves enforcement when wired; lines 228-242 prove no verifier means no proof required.
exploitability: A compromised first-party signed process, stolen daemon token, or local process that can satisfy existing daemon admission could request Computer Use without the independent phone/device proof boundary.
impact: High-impact local browser actions could execute under weaker authorization than claimed.
recommendation: Wire DaemonLocalAuthProofVerifier in the production executable, back it with a persistent pinned-key/replay store, and fail closed for Computer Use when proof material is unavailable.
acceptanceCriteria: Production daemon startup has a non-nil verifier; Computer Use start/invoke fail without valid proof; stale, wrong-device, wrong-intent, replayed, and unsigned proofs are rejected.
regressionTest: Add a production-configuration test that constructs the executable/server path and asserts missing proof is rejected.

title: Daemon browser Computer Use uses synthetic entitlement and kill-switch context
affectedAsset: ASSET-008 Computer Use approvals and audit chain
description: The daemon Computer Use context sets killSwitch to false and returns an always-active browser entitlement. The common capability gate enforces kill switch and entitlement only from the supplied context.
evidence: OpenBurnBarDaemon/Sources/OpenBurnBarDaemon/ComputerUse/ComputerUseService.swift:108-149 builds the action context with killSwitch false.
OpenBurnBarDaemon/Sources/OpenBurnBarDaemon/ComputerUse/ComputerUseService.swift:285-310 returns synthetic active browser entitlement.
OpenBurnBarCore/Sources/OpenBurnBarComputerUseCore/ComputerUseCapabilityGate.swift:232-246 enforces kill-switch and entitlement decisions from context.
exploitability: If a user is suspended, entitlement expires, or the remote kill switch is enabled, daemon-owned browser action flow may not observe that state.
impact: Safety and commercial enforcement claims are weaker for daemon browser Computer Use.
recommendation: Replace synthetic context with the same live entitlement and Remote Config source used by app-mediated Computer Use.
acceptanceCriteria: Daemon Computer Use denies action when kill switch is active or entitlement is inactive, with tests for both cases.
regressionTest: Add daemon ComputerUseService tests with killSwitch true and inactive entitlement.

title: Stripe redirect URL validation accepts unsafe non-HTTPS localhost-substring hosts
description: The shared boundedHttpsURL helper rejects a URL only when protocol is not HTTPS and the hostname does not include localhost. That allows non-HTTPS hostnames containing the substring localhost, such as localhost attacker domains.
evidence: functions/src/callables/shared/validators.ts:344-356 implements boundedHttpsURL with hostname.includes('localhost').
functions/src/callables/stripe.ts:229-254 uses boundedHttpsURL for checkout success and cancel URLs.
functions/src/callables/stripe.ts:314-341 uses boundedHttpsURL for portal return URLs.
exploitability: An authenticated client can request Stripe redirects to an attacker-controlled non-HTTPS host that contains localhost in the hostname.
impact: Phishing, callback confusion, or token leakage if future clients attach sensitive state to return URLs.
existingControls: Auth and App Check on callables
recommendation: Use exact loopback detection for local development, require HTTPS for all non-loopback hosts, and consider an allowlist of production return origins.
acceptanceCriteria: http://localhost and http://127.0.0.1 are accepted only in dev/test where intended; http://localhost.attacker.example and any non-HTTPS non-loopback URL are rejected.
regressionTest: Add unit tests for boundedHttpsURL and Stripe callable redirect validation.

title: Firestore App Check enforcement is deployment-state dependent and not repo-verifiable
affectedComponent: Firestore rules and Firebase production configuration
affectedAsset: ASSET-009 Firestore and Storage user data
description: Firestore rules document that App Check must be enforced in Firebase console, and code comments confirm Firestore rules do not use request.app. The repository cannot prove production App Check enforcement for direct Firestore access.
evidence: firestore.rules:20-23 says App Check enforcement for Firestore rules is configured in Firebase console.
functions/src/appCheckAttestation.ts:1-8 notes Firestore rules do not use request.app.
functions/src/config.ts:384-399 fail closed for Functions App Check but not Firestore deployment state.
exploitability: If production App Check drifts off, owner-scoped Firestore rules still require Auth but do not independently require app attestation.
impact: Compromised credentials or scripted clients have a larger direct Firestore attack surface than claimed.
recommendation: Add an ops verifier that queries Firebase production App Check enforcement state and gates release/readiness on the expected value.
acceptanceCriteria: Release gate fails if Firestore App Check enforcement is off or unknown; audit output records the verified production project and timestamp.
regressionTest: Add a mocked Firebase/GCP API verifier test and include the verifier in ops readiness.

title: Public HTTP endpoints lack explicit product-layer rate limiting evidence
description: Public endpoints are intentionally unauthenticated for health, discovery, CLI link, webhook, and rundown flows. Some handlers rely on request validation and maxInstances, but repository evidence for explicit IP/userless token-bucket or edge rate limiting is incomplete.
evidence: functions/src/security/endpointAuthorizationCatalog.generated.ts lists public or not-applicable HTTP/webhook endpoints.
functions/src/routerRundown.ts:205-220 configures latestRouterRundown with cors true and maxInstances 10.
services/hosted-mcp/src/rateLimits.ts:5-36 shows strong rate limiting for hosted MCP authenticated flows, but not for every public Function endpoint.
exploitability: Unauthenticated clients can repeatedly hit public endpoints unless edge controls outside the repo stop them.
impact: Denial-of-wallet, noisy logs, and availability degradation.
recommendation: Add explicit public endpoint rate limits or prove enforced Cloud Armor/Firebase edge limits in release verification.
acceptanceCriteria: Every public endpoint has a rate-limit control, signature requirement, or documented non-sensitive low-cost bound with tests.
regressionTest: Add unit tests around public rate-limit middleware and a CI inventory check for public endpoints.

title: Data deletion audit logging is best-effort
affectedAsset: ASSET-013 Audit logs and ASSET-009 user data
description: Data export uses fail-closed audit append, but deletion catches audit failures and still completes. That is a product decision, but it weakens non-repudiation for irreversible privacy actions.
evidence: functions/src/callables/dataDeletion.ts:105-113 catches audit append failure and still returns deletion results.
functions/src/callables/auditLog.ts:171-184 provides appendAuditEventRequired for fail-closed high-risk actions.
functions/src/callables/dataExport.ts:606-660 uses high-risk proof and required audit for export.
exploitability: A transient audit write failure during deletion could leave no durable record of an irreversible action.
impact: Weaker incident response, compliance evidence, and user support investigation.
recommendation: Use a required pre-delete audit intent plus completion record, or make deletion fail closed when audit persistence fails.
acceptanceCriteria: Every successful deletion has a durable audit intent record and best-effort or required completion record.
regressionTest: Add a test that simulates audit failure and verifies the selected fail-closed or pre-intent behavior.

title: Production deploy still supports long-lived secret fallback paths
affectedAsset: ASSET-010 CI secrets and release artifacts
description: The production deploy workflow has OIDC permissions but still includes service-account JSON and legacy Firebase token fallback paths. That increases blast radius if repository or Actions secrets are compromised.
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:3-6 enables id-token and read permissions.
.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:109-119 supports service-account JSON fallback.
.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:193-201 supports FIREBASE_TOKEN fallback.
exploitability: An attacker with access to long-lived deploy secrets can deploy without the stronger OIDC/WIF trust boundary.
impact: Release integrity and production control-plane compromise risk.
recommendation: Move production deploy to WIF/OIDC only and remove long-lived deploy token fallback paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Workflow fails if WIF is unavailable; no FIREBASE_TOKEN or service-account JSON is needed for production deploy.
regressionTest: Add a static CI policy that blocks production deploy workflows from referencing FIREBASE_TOKEN or service-account JSON secrets.

title: SQLCipher key creation can continue after Keychain persistence failure
affectedAsset: ASSET-002 Local encryption keys and ASSET-004 session data
description: If a newly generated SQLCipher key fails to persist to Keychain, the service logs the failure but returns the key. That can create a database encrypted with a non-persisted key and cause future availability/recovery failures.
evidence: AgentLens/Services/DataStore/DatabaseEncryptionService.swift:95-117 generates a key, attempts SecItemAdd, logs failure, and returns the key.
exploitability: This is mainly an availability and support risk, not a broad confidentiality bypass.
impact: Encrypted local data can become unrecoverable after app restart if Keychain persistence failed.
recommendation: Fail closed when Keychain persistence fails for a new database key.
acceptanceCriteria: No encrypted database is created with a key that was not successfully persisted or explicitly exported through a recovery path.
regressionTest: Inject SecItemAdd failure and assert database open/setup fails with a recoverable error.

title: Signal and E2EE privacy claims require narrower wording
affectedComponent: Cloud Vault and public security wording
affectedAsset: ASSET-004 conversations, prompts, model outputs, and session logs
description: The code supports AES-GCM Cloud Vault envelopes and a Signal envelope type, but the Signal envelope is additive, flag-gated, and not the default production write path for all Cloud Vault data. Broad Signal-quality or universal E2EE claims are not defensible.
evidence: OpenBurnBarCore/Sources/OpenBurnBarCore/SharedModels/CloudVaultCrypto.swift:202-223 describes Signal envelopes as additive, flag-off, and not default production writes.
OpenBurnBarCore/Sources/OpenBurnBarCore/SharedModels/CloudVaultCrypto.swift:31-82 and 470-486 support context-bound AES-GCM sealed text.
exploitability: This is a claim and trust risk rather than a direct exploit.
impact: User misunderstanding, enterprise procurement failure, and audit finding if public claims exceed implementation.
recommendation: Use precise claim language: AES-GCM Cloud Vault with context-bound AAD today; Signal envelopes only for specific enabled flows.
acceptanceCriteria: Security docs, product copy, and auditor brief avoid broad Signal-quality or universal E2EE claims unless a flow-specific proof and test exist.
regressionTest: Add a claim-lint or documentation review gate for prohibited E2EE wording.
